explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strong, non-monotonic effect on predicted bike demand. Demand is heavily suppressed in the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 a.m.), with the deepest negative contribution around 4–5 a.m. It then rises sharply through the morning, reaching a first peak around 8 a.m., dips slightly in mid-morning, holds at moderate positive levels through midday, and climbs to its highest point around 5–6 p.m. before falling off again late at night.

[IMPORTANCE] This is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9 with an importance score of 0.889. The hour of day drives larger swings in predicted demand than any other variable, including weather or season.

[RECOMMENDATION] Ensure maximum bike availability and staff coverage during the two daily peak windows — around 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m. — while reducing resources in the early-morning hours (roughly 1–5 a.m.) when demand is at its lowest.
